question: How Do I Export WooCommerce Subscription Data to Accounting Software?
metaDescription: A dedicated sync plugin handles it best for ongoing use — manual CSV export works for a one-off, but neither is automatic out of the box.
shortAnswer: WooCommerce doesn't export directly to accounting software on its own, but renewal orders are regular WooCommerce orders underneath, so any tool that exports orders can be pointed at them. For ongoing, automatic bookkeeping, a dedicated sync plugin built for the specific accounting platform (QuickBooks, Xero, and similar) is the practical approach; for a one-off export, WooCommerce's built-in order CSV export covers renewal orders the same as regular ones.

bodyHtml:
How It Actually Works

Every subscription renewal produces a genuine WooCommerce order, complete with line items, tax, and payment details, indistinguishable in the orders table from any other order except for the meta linking it back to its parent subscription. That means any export or accounting-sync tool built for WooCommerce orders in general already covers subscription renewals — there's no separate "subscription data" format to deal with.

Choosing the Right Approach

  • A dedicated accounting-sync plugin (built specifically for QuickBooks, Xero, or a similar platform) is worth it for ongoing use — it typically syncs automatically as new orders (including renewals) come in, maps tax and product categories to the right accounts, and handles refunds/partial refunds correctly.
  • Built-in CSV export under WooCommerce → Orders → Export covers a one-off historical export well, including renewal orders, but doesn't run automatically or map fields to a specific accounting platform's expected format.
  • Volume matters — a store with a handful of subscriptions can manage with periodic manual export, while one with hundreds of active subscriptions generating renewals daily needs an automatic sync to avoid a growing manual reconciliation burden.
  • Tax handling specifics (different rates across renewal periods, refunds on renewals) need to be mapped correctly in whichever tool is used, since accounting software often expects a stricter structure than a raw CSV export provides by default.

Setting It Up

  1. Identify the accounting platform in use and search specifically for a WooCommerce integration built for it, rather than a generic CSV importer.
  2. For occasional needs, use WooCommerce's built-in order export, filtering by date range, and map the columns manually in the accounting software's import tool.
  3. For ongoing automatic sync, install and configure the dedicated integration plugin, testing against a handful of real renewal orders before relying on it fully.
  4. Reconcile a sample period manually after setup to confirm renewal orders, refunds, and taxes are all mapping correctly before trusting it long-term.

Need a custom accounting export or integration built for a specific platform? See custom WooCommerce development.
